subject: POC Sprint Outline & Next Steps — Avery Systems
messages:
From: Sylvia Turner <sylvia.turner@averysystems.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: technical constraints & high-level goals

Monica / Karthik — thanks again for the demo and for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned before a kickoff: 

Key pain points we described on the call:
- Intermittent p99 latency spikes on the customer chat flow (spikes up to ~1.2s when concurrency ramps at 2x peak).
- Cost unpredictability for nightly batch summary jobs — monthly token spend varies widely and is hard to forecast.
- Retrieval-augmented summaries sometimes hallucinate company-specific entities; we need higher factuality.
- Data residency: EU customer data must stay in our EU region for a subset of workloads.

Primary goals for a pilot (we proposed):
- Demonstrate stable interactive latencies: p99 < 300ms for the live chat endpoint under expected load.
- Reduce per-token cost for batch summaries by ~30% vs current baseline.
- Build an eval suite (500 prompt pairs) to measure hallucination rate / factuality and acceptance criteria.
- Validate routing/fallback policies for EU-only datasets.

Suggested scope & timeline idea: 6-week pilot focusing on 2 endpoints (interactive chat + nightly summarization). Deliverables: baseline metrics, prompt/eval suite, config recommendations, and cost/latency delta report.

Asks from us to get started quickly:
1) Example dataset (S3 link or CSV) with ~1k representative examples and any existing prompt templates.
2) Access matrix for the three teams we’ll need (engineering, SRE, security) — names and email addresses.
3) Any procurement timeline or constraints we should be aware of.

Attaching: call notes + rough draft of Mutual Action Plan we can iterate on (will accept a redline).

We’re excited to move forward — happy to kickoff next week if that works for your org.

— Sylvia
Director, AI Product
Avery Systems

Attachments: call_recording_0907.mp4 (link stub), sample-issue-trace.txt

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: technical constraints & high-level goals

Thanks Sylvia — this is a clear summary and aligns with what we captured on our side. I’ve sketched a short kickoff plan below and attached a Mutual Action Plan (MAP_Avery_20260907.xlsx) for sign-off. Please review and tell us any edits.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Tech kickoff (60–90m): Wed 9/9 or Thu 9/10 — objective: architecture walk, access checklist, and success metrics. Please confirm preferred time.
- We’ll run a baseline collection (2–3 days) against your current endpoints to capture p50/p95/p99 and token burn for the sample set.
- Rdw owners: Monica (sales lead / single-threaded owner), Marissa (solutions eng — will lead integration and evals), Karthik (account exec / commercial).

POC scope (detailed):
- Week 0: Access + baseline collection (logs, sample prompt set).
- Week 1–2: Interactive endpoint tuning (latency SLOs, batching config, prefix caching).
- Week 3–4: Batch summarization optimization (quantization recommendations, batching, cost measurement).
- Week 5: Eval run with 500-prompt suite (relevance/factuality scoring).
- Week 6: Handoff + recommendations + cost/latency report.

Success metrics (examples we’ll track):
- p99 latency (interactive): target < 300ms under expected load.
- Token cost delta (batch): target >= 30% reduction vs baseline.
- Hallucination rate (eval): < X% (we’ll define threshold together).

Access we need for initial work:
- Temporary S3 read access to sample data (or secure file share).
- API keys / test endpoints (read-only) or a staging deploy if available.
- List of internal contacts and an Okta SAML admin if you want us to test SSO.

I attached the MAP and a short checklist (poc-checklist.pdf) — Marissa will send a more detailed integration checklist after the kickoff. If the 9/9/9:30am PDT slot works we’ll send a calendar invite.

Looking forward — Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

- Paperwork: we can proceed on our standard POC addendum (I’ll attach RDW-AVY-quote-v1.pdf) and accept your PO if that’s your preference.
- Deal id: RDW-2026-AVY-003 — reference this on any procurement docs.
- Security: if you need a security review looped in, we’ll engage our security lead (internal) for an evidence package (SOC2, data handling, encryption-at-rest).

Next steps for procurement: please share the procurement contact (email) and any required contract template. If procurement wants to review the MAP before kickoff we can pause scheduling, but we’re happy to run the tech kickoff in parallel to keep momentum.
